title: A dense open in a finite type scheme over a field has full dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec} k$ be locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $U\subseteq Y$ is a dense open subset, then $\dim Y\le\dim U$, where both dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $U$ has its subspace topology. Together with subspace monotonicity this is equality. No irreducibility, reducedness, equidimensionality, or nonemptiness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0BXV, lemma-dim-1-projective-completion, dimension sentence; its cited Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic. Already proved in lean/WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/DenseCompactification.lean, theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_of_dense.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes Y Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The finite irreducible components [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] have generic points by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. Every point x specializes from a component generic point eta. Such eta lies in U: remove the closures of the other finitely many component generic points to get an open neighbourhood of eta, use density of U there, and use stability of opens under generalization. This is the proved source helper mem_of_dense_of_forall_specializes_eq.

Give the closure of eta its reduced induced closed subscheme structure T by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is integral, locally of finite type over k, and its inverse image of U is nonempty because eta belongs to U. By [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension], T has the dimension of that nonempty open. The closed immersion identifies this open with a subspace of U, so its dimension is at most dim U. Every specialization chain ending below eta is contained in the closure of eta. Taking the supremum over x, using [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], gives dim Y at most dim U. The empty case has no x and the supremum is bottom. This is precisely the complete existing Lean proof of topologicalKrullDim_le_of_dense, reused rather than restated.
